items.q: A business has revenue of £760,000 and receivables of £70,000. What are its receivables days?
items.why: Receivables days = receivables ÷ revenue × 365 = £70,000 ÷ £760,000 × 365 = 33.6, about 34 days.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has non-current liabilities of £200,000 and a gearing ratio of 40%. It then takes out a long-term loan of £100,000. Calculate its new gearing.
items.why: Capital employed = £200,000 ÷ 0.40 = £500,000. The loan adds £100,000 to both non-current liabilities and capital employed: £300,000 ÷ £600,000 × 100 = 50%.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2019 Q17

items.q: A noodle bar breaks even at 400 meals/week. Fixed costs = £800/week, price = £5 per meal. The variable cost per meal is:
items.why: At break-even: TR = TC. TR = 400 x 5 = 2000. TC = 800 + (400 x VC). So 2000 = 800 + 400VC. 1200 = 400VC. VC = £3. Alternative method: Contribution x 400 = 800 (FC). CPU = £2.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business budgeted income of £85m and expenditure of £79m. Actual income was 5% below budget and actual expenditure was 5% below budget. What is the profit variance?
items.why: Budgeted profit = £85m – £79m = £6m. Actual income = £80.75m, actual expenditure = £75.05m, so actual profit = £5.70m. Variance = £5.70m – £6m = £0.30m adverse (profit is lower than budgeted).
items.label: New question

items.q: The chart shows the inventory of a component over nine days. The business has a reorder quantity of 90 units and a lead time of 2 days. On which day was an incorrect quantity ordered?
items.why: The delivery on day 6 only lifts inventory from 30 to 90 units, which is 60 units, not 90. With a lead time of 2 days, that order was placed on day 4. Day 6 is when it arrived, not when it was ordered.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2019 Q11

items.q: Fixed costs are £16,500, the selling price is £12 and variable costs are £7 per unit. The business currently sells 4,000 units. What is its margin of safety?
items.why: Break-even = £16,500 ÷ (£12 – £7) = 3,300 units. Margin of safety = actual output – break-even output = 4,000 – 3,300 = 700 units. The answer is in units, not pounds.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has a gross profit margin of 40% on revenue of £85m. What is its cost of sales?
items.why: Gross profit = 40% × £85m = £34m. Cost of sales = revenue – gross profit = £85m – £34m = £51m.
items.label: New question

items.q: A factory with 75 employees produced 87,000 units last year. What was its labour productivity?
items.why: Labour productivity = output ÷ number of employees = 87,000 ÷ 75 = 1,160 units per employee per year.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company has non-current liabilities of £60m and total equity of £90m. What is its gearing?
items.why: Capital employed = total equity + non-current liabilities = £90m + £60m = £150m. Gearing = non-current liabilities ÷ capital employed × 100 = 60 ÷ 150 × 100 = 40%.
items.label: New question

items.q: Marks and Spencer plc, 1 April 2017 (£m): current assets 1,723; current liabilities 2,368. Calculate its current ratio.
items.why: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 1,723 ÷ 2,368 = 0.73:1.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2018 Q01.3
